@@ -579,27 +609,29 @@ endif::[]
 [#section_cap_integrity]
 === Integrity of Capabilities
 
-CHERI enforces the following rules for all valid capabilities:
+CHERI enforces the following rules (integrity checks) for all valid capabilities :
 
 . The bounds are not <<section_cap_malformed,malformed>>.
 . The capability metadata does not have any bits, or fields set to a reserved value.
 .. An example of a reserved field value is permissions which cannot be legally produced by <<CLRPERM>>.
 
-Since a capability with the {ctag} set that fails integrity checks could not have been legally created, such a failure indicates either
+If any of the above rules do not hold for a capability with the {ctag} set, it indicates either:
 
 * State corruption due to memory or logic faults, or
 * The presence of incompatible or faulty CHERI IP within the system.
 
 NOTE: These checks are much less rigorous than parity or ECC protection, and are only
 used to detect simple problems with the capability metadata.
 
+Performing these checks is optional except for instructions that are defined to accept arbitrary input bit patterns and can write an output with the {ctag} set.
+All instructions that require integrity checks have this noted in the instruction description.
+
+NOTE: Currently <<CBLD>> is the only defined instruction that sets the `{ctag}` on an arbitrary bit pattern and therefore _must_ perform an integrity check on the input capability in `{cs2}`.
+For all other instructions, a malformed input capability can only be triggered by glitches in the system and therefore performing these checks is optional unless the hart implements additional reliability features.
body: I'm not sure about the word `glitches`, as it doesn't cover incompatible CHERI IPs - which is probably the most liekly source of reserved bits being set.
